units.account: Col. Aubry has no order and holds his line facing the bridge. He sees the 2nd Battalion march off along the river bank to the east and supposes it has its reasons. Nothing of the enemy is in sight.

Col. Delacroix gets his order at about the sixth minute. The written figure is blotted, and he reads it as 3,000 paces rather than 300. Cautious, he reads it twice, but the order says extend the line east and watch for a crossing downstream, so he forms column and marches east along the south bank to carry it out, and is still marching at the end of the turn, over a kilometre from the 1st Battalion.
units.departure: The projection takes the order as written: 300 paces east, to (2400,1680), where the battalion halts. The courier's order is garbled, and the colonel reads 3,000 paces instead of 300, so he marches the 1,400 m that the rest of the turn allows, ending at (3540,1680) and still moving, more than a kilometre from the projected position.

units.account: Maj. Verneuil has no order and holds behind the infantry. He sees the 2nd Battalion march away to the east and is puzzled, but does not stir without orders.
Col. Brandt is told to stand fast and does, in line facing south, chafing.
Col. Hartmann has no order and holds his position, by the book.
Maj. von Reiter has no order and holds his position.

summary: Blue-2 got the order to extend the line east along the river bank and watch for a crossing downstream, but it came in garbled. Col. Delacroix read '300 paces' as '3,000' and marched east in column from about minute 6, covering about 1,400 m to (3540,1680) and still marching, so the Blue line at the bridge is now held by the 1st Battalion with the cavalry behind. Red-1 stood fast; all the other units held. No contact: Red is still 1,400 m or more from Blue's infantry, and nobody saw anybody.
